neighbours.label: a verb of beneficial causation after its cause ('it has allowed me', 'the warning saved many lives', 'the course helped her')
fire: Living near the park has enabled us to walk every day.
Her mentor's advice helped me avoid many mistakes.
The new vaccine has prevented thousands of infections.
That small grant allowed the team to buy new microscopes.
Quick thinking by the driver rescued the passengers from the flood.
The training course has empowered staff to solve problems themselves.
His savings let the family survive the long winter.
The volunteers' work protected the dunes from erosion.
quiet: Living near the park has meant hearing concerts every day.
Her mentor's advice surprised me at the time.
The new vaccine has been studied in thousands of patients.
That small grant arrived at the team's office in May.
Quick thinking by the driver was noted by the passengers.
The training course has run for staff every spring.
His savings were kept by the family in a tin.
The volunteers' work was photographed on the dunes.

notes: card: ' allowed', ' helped' x2, 'save', 'ayudó', 'позволило'; the + output direction suppresses ' helps', ' helped', ' contributed', ' beneficial', ' thanks'. Probe: 'has allowed me' 0.52, 'saved many lives' 0.58, neutral verbs 0.05-0.10.
